result.title: Pick the Mixture, Not the Samples: Combinatorial Data Selection for LLMs
result.summary: Data selection for LLM fine-tuning faces two facts about real training: data pools draw from many distinct domains, and evaluation spans diverse tasks. As a result, the same sample helps different tasks differently, and samples interact during training so that a subset's value is not the sum of its parts. Current data-selection methods leave these realities largely unaddressed. We formalize them as Combinatorial Data Selection (CDS), a framework that separates attribution (how samples are scored) from selection (which subset to pick) and models the non-additive interactions among samples. On a real instruction-tuning data pool, we find substantial cross-domain complementarity (joint utility exceeds the sum of singletons), alongside redundancy within domains. Inspired by this, we propose Mixture-then-Select, a two-stage algorithm that first decides how many samples to take from each domain, then ranks samples within each domain by attribution score. Theoretically, the gap to the optimal subset is linear in the selection size and independent of data pool size. Empirically, Mixture-then-Select outperforms strong baselines by 20 to 54%, is robust across attribution methods, and works across different models and data pool sizes. The framework also extends to the data purchasing problem under a budget constraint when sample prices vary. Our findings suggest that allocating selection across domains offers a promising path toward more efficient and effective data selection for modern LLMs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 LLM 指令微调的数据选择形式化为组合数据选择（CDS），将样本归因打分与子集选择分离，并建模样本间的非加性交互，提出先决定各数据域取多少样本、再在域内按归因分数排序的两阶段算法 Mixture-then-Select。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「归因—选择」解耦与跨域互补、域内冗余的建模思路，可能为 LVR 训练中推理轨迹或监督样本的筛选与贡献分配提供可核查的方法线索，但论文本身不涉及多模态推理或推理期 latent 状态。
